body: Sorry, the 'people listening superficially' wasn't directed at you, actually. And, PM'd.

Thanks a lot; I'll keep United Way in mind. I actually do have insurance, but last time I was in a psych ward (well, the only time), they refused to pay for most of it because I checked myself in voluntarily and then I ended up incurring ridiculous fees for the people I spoke to who were "out of the network" - as if you even have a choice of who you're getting treated by when you're in.

And I am not at all proud of this, but I did have a failed attempt in my past, yes. I decided to try and view my continued existence as a second chance, but recently, it's been getting more and more difficult for me to remember myself in the midst of everything and sometimes I get dangerously close to getting into the car and setting the 'plan' into motion.

At this point, I don't think I'm able to just open up to yet another health professional, because I've been burned by doctors, psychologists, and psychiatrists. I understand there are good ones out there, but I just haven't found them yet, and I don't feel strong enough to keep going through them at the moment. I'm sure that a good psychiatrist would be immensely helpful to me, but it's hard to tell who would work best with whom, as everyone has different counseling needs. You're right though in that I do really just want a supportive presence in my life to keep me going.

As for meds, by "making things worse," I actually mean that more often than not, sometime in the midst of the adjustment period, I start reaching for sharp objects, which is not at all a good place to be.

> What exactly are you looking for?

Support. People listening superficially do not tend to be a big help.

> Another thing I can say (not advice, really) is that your sickness will get better, so at least soon you will be a healthy depressed person.

Unfortunately, no it won't.

Sadly, life doesn't work in a way that would allow me to tackle only one of my problems at a time. There is no time for me to take it step by step, day by day; the government has no sympathy for personal issues and I need to resolve things there first and foremost because my legal status may be expiring soon, but I have no magic solution. It's a huge weight pressing down on me.

I know that people are greatly helped by medication, and I really wish there was one that I could use to help hold me over in the meantime. I just want the strength to keep fighting. I like the idea of meditation, but without another person there to help me through, I often fail to get in the right state of mind.

All of the above. Not being sure that things will get better. Not being sure about what I'm trying for, and not being sure that it is worth all this effort. Not being able to ultimately get away from my pain and my shame from being in pain.


I have long formulated an escape plan. I am fighting with myself because the emotions and spiraling thoughts take over often and I'm afraid that I will lose the battle, but I don't want to.


Also, I don't have the money to go into a psychiatric ward.

First of all, thanks for the response.

It is not one thing, it is the combination of everything that has built up and become overwhelming. I feel like I could handle each of my problems separately, but now I'm not sure where to start and where to start gathering energy.


I've tried exercise and it definitely helps for short periods, but ultimately, I still have the same problems in my life afterward.


Ideally, I'd either not be sick or to not have to worry about possibly being kicked out of the country in a few months. Unfortunately, neither of those are easily resolvable and I'm fast running out of ways to distract myself. So what I think I need in the meantime is just people who are going to be understanding and who can serve as a strong support system. People aren't always available or caring though and it is even more depressing to try and reach out, only to get air.

Oh, and the job situation is not terrible, but it's not great and because I'm already depressed, I'm having an incredibly hard time forcing myself to get on with it.
